I have been farming this land in Quzhou for 20 years. I know what works here. The soil is good, the well gives me water when I need it, and I have 4 mouths to feed plus I need cash income. My maize feeds my family and sells locally. My stevia is the cash crop — the companies come and buy it, and it earns more per mu than maize.

For the maize, I plant summer maize like always — after the last frost, get it in the ground in June. I use hybrid seed because over the years I have seen it yields more than the old varieties. I know the right amount of fertilizer from experience — I put down base fertilizer before planting, then top-dress urea when the corn is knee-high. I irrigate at planting, at tasseling, and at grain fill — three times is enough with my well if rain comes normally. I spray for corn borer and aphids, twice is usually enough.

For the stevia, I plant it in spring. It is thirsty and needs more water than the maize. I irrigate more frequently. The company rep has told me the improved varieties give better leaf yield, so I use those. I harvest twice — once in July and once before frost in September. Stevia needs potassium, I have learned this over the years, so I put more potash on it.

I split my land roughly: 40 mu maize for food security and reliable income, 17 mu stevia for the better cash return.
